topic: Bolivia lost its Pacific coast to Chile in the War of the Pacific (1879–1884, Treaty of 1904), keeps a navy based on Lake Titicaca and inland rivers, marks the Day of the Sea on 23 March, and lost its 2018 ICJ case asking Chile to negotiate sea access.
policy_note: Every spoken or shown fact → a claim with ≥ 2 independent publishers; core claims need a primary/scholarly source.

myths.reality: It had about 400 km of Pacific coast (the Litoral department, Antofagasta) from independence in 1825 until 1879.

guardrails.why: Contested name — say 'the Gulf' or use both names (docs/BORDER_POLICY.md).
Sovereignty language on disputed areas is banned; say administers / claims.

brit_wotp.title: War of the Pacific (1879–84)
brit_wotp.notes: Chile against Bolivia and Peru, 1879–84; Bolivia lost its coastal province (Antofagasta) and became landlocked; 1904 treaty confirmed Chilean sovereignty.

brit_bolivia.title: Bolivia — Independence and the War of the Pacific
brit_bolivia.notes: Bolivia's Litoral on the Pacific, roughly 400 km of coast, lost to Chile after 1879.

icj2018.title: Obligation to Negotiate Access to the Pacific Ocean (Bolivia v. Chile), Judgment of 1 October 2018
icj2018.notes: The Court found that Chile did not undertake a legal obligation to negotiate a sovereign access to the Pacific Ocean for Bolivia (12 votes to 3).

reuters_icj.title: World Court rules Chile not obliged to negotiate sea access for Bolivia (1 Oct 2018)
reuters_icj.notes: ICJ ruled against Bolivia; Bolivia lost its 400 km coast in the 1879–83 war.

treaty1904.title: Treaty of Peace and Friendship of 1904 between Chile and Bolivia
treaty1904.notes: Signed 20 October 1904; Bolivia recognised Chilean sovereignty over the former Litoral; Chile granted transit rights and built the Arica–La Paz railway.

bbc_navy.title: Bolivia's landlocked navy dreams of the sea (2018)
bbc_navy.notes: Bolivia's navy, about 5,000 personnel, patrols Lake Titicaca and the rivers; the 23 March Día del Mar; the ICJ case.

armada.title: Armada Boliviana — Historia y misión
armada.notes: Official site of the Bolivian Navy: mission, river and lake districts, Lake Titicaca naval base (Tiquina).

wiki_navy.title: Bolivian Navy
wiki_navy.notes: Armada Boliviana, about 5,000 personnel, headquartered in La Paz, bases on Lake Titicaca and the river systems.

wiki_dia.title: Día del Mar
wiki_dia.notes: Day of the Sea, 23 March, commemorating the loss of the coast (Battle of Topáter, 1879).

brit_titicaca.title: Lake Titicaca
brit_titicaca.notes: Elevation about 3,810 m; on the Peru–Bolivia border; the highest large navigable lake.

claims.text: Bolivia is landlocked and maintains a navy of roughly 5,000 personnel operating on Lake Titicaca and its rivers.
vo: bolivia has a navy. it has not had a coastline for more than a century
so where does the navy sail? up here, on lake titicaca, nearly four kilometres up in the andes, with around five thousand sailors and a fleet of patrol boats
a navy without a sea, drilling on a mountain lake, waiting for a coast it still calls its own

claims.text: Bolivia held about 400 km of Pacific coast (the Litoral, around Antofagasta) until 1879.
vo: this is the pacific shore bolivia once held, a long desert coast around antofagasta

claims.text: In the War of the Pacific (1879–84) Chile took the coast; the 1904 treaty fixed Chilean sovereignty and Bolivia became landlocked.

claims.text: Bolivia marks the Day of the Sea every 23 March and in 2018 the ICJ ruled Chile has no obligation to negotiate sea access.
vo: bolivia never accepted it. every march it marks the day of the sea, with parades far from any shore, and in 2018 it took chile to the world court, asking for a way back to the ocean. it lost
screen: Chile has no duty to negotiate
